settings.toneNote: funny in the way real cramped misery is funny — never quirky-cute

concept.summary: Seventeen-year-old Nell Prager books the cheapest cross-country rideshare on the internet to get from her mother's house in Ohio to a sister she barely knows in Portland — four days in a sagging sedan with three strangers: the driver who isn't licensed to carry passengers, a divorcée transporting her ex-husband's ashes without permission, and a college dropout who says he's going home but keeps changing where home is. Nell told each of them a different story about who she is. There are three states left to cross when the stories start colliding.

characters.name: Nell Prager
characters.backstory: Raised by a mother who reinvents herself with every new boyfriend and every new town. Nell has moved nine times; she packs in eleven minutes.
characters.motivations: Get to Portland and become someone with no history.
characters.flaws: Lies reflexively, brilliantly, and about nothing that matters.
characters.want: A clean start with the sister who got out first.
characters.need: To stop treating her own history as evidence against her.
characters.voice: deadpan, too fast, tests adults with small lies
characters.arc: From curating versions of herself to letting one be seen whole.

characters.name: Dot Marsh
characters.backstory: Divorced eleven years; taking her ex-husband's ashes to the lake he loved, without telling his widow.
characters.motivations: Finish one thing on her own terms.
characters.need: To grieve the marriage, not just the man.
characters.voice: flat Midwest understatement, devastating when direct
